memos.risk:
Risk call on REP: I'd refuse the buy at any size.

Reasons: the classifier says ORGANIC, but the curve shows 76% bundle share, which is a bundled-launch signature, not organic demand. The first 2 minutes after graduation had a launch bot present and a sell-to-buy ratio above 1 (1.07), so early flow was net selling. The last 15 minutes are net-positive only by 32 SOL against 530 SOL of buys, with 759 sellers against 909 buyers, so the exit pressure is heavy. The pool is 116.5 SOL deep, thin enough that a $20 round trip costs at the high end of the 1.4-5.1% range, and a 20-50% stop would be hit by normal volatility given the 30-minute return of +117% followed by a 7.7% pullback.

If the desk overrides and buys anyway: $5 ticket (the minimum), stop at 20%, hold no longer than 15-30 minutes, and exit immediately if the sell flow stays above buy flow. I'd still expect this to be a negative-expectancy trade, so the default should be skip.
memos.scout:
The strongest case for buying REP is breadth of participation. Over the last 15 minutes it logged 909 buyers and 529 SOL of buy flow against 497 SOL of sells, a 48% return, and 30-minute return is +117%. Top-3 and top-5 buyer concentration are low (8.6% and 14%), there is no airdrop-dump pattern, and the coin is classed ORGANIC. Post-graduation flow was roughly balanced (sell/buy ratio 1.07), and the drawdown from its 30-minute high is only 7.7%, so it has not broken down. Pool depth of 116.5 SOL is adequate for a $20 ticket.

The honest caveats are significant. Bundle share is 76%, which suggests much of the buying came through coordinated or bundled transactions rather than independent demand, and a launch bot was present. Net flow over the window is only +32.6 SOL on about 1,000 SOL of gross volume, so most activity is churn. Whether the 909 buyers persist into the 30-60 minute window is unknown, and the base rate for buying alive coins in this age band is negative. Demand looks real on the surface but is not clearly durable, so this is a weak case for a buy rather than a strong one.
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss path: insider distribution into retail flow. The curve shows bundle_share of 0.7631, meaning about three-quarters of activity came through bundled transactions, and the completer_share of 0.363 suggests a large slice of supply was accumulated by a few wallets that finished the bonding curve. The first two minutes after graduation show a launch bot present and a sell-to-buy ratio of 1.073, so sells already outpaced buys in the earliest window. Last 15 minutes: 759 sellers against 909 buyers, sell_sol of 496.9 against buy_sol of 529.52, and a net flow of only 32.62 SOL on a 0.48 return. That thin net flow on heavy two-way volume looks like exit liquidity being passed around. A 7.7% drawdown from the 30-minute high is already underway, and with a 116.5 SOL pool, a 2-5% round-trip cost means a modest bounce can't cover fees. Skip.
